context: Bee swarm plot of 500 companies by annual revenue ($100K–$1B) on a log scale, with 6 sector categories encoded by color (Tol palette), a box plot summary strip below, and a Log/Linear/Symlog scale toggle that re-runs a force simulation to reposition dots.
first_impression: The log-scale swarm is immediately readable — the distribution shape is clear, dots are well-separated, and the box plot anchors the statistical summary cleanly.
what_works: The collision-resolved force layout at r=4 keeps 500 dots from overlapping, making the density shape legible across the full 4-decade range; the 6-color Tol palette is colorblind-safe and hover-to-dim interaction effectively isolates individual companies without needing the user to parse a crowded legend.
what_doesnt: The swarm occupies only the top ~55% of the SVG height, leaving a large dead zone between the dots and the box plot that wastes vertical space and makes the chart feel unbalanced; with 500 dots in 6 intermixed colors spanning the full axis, sector-level pattern detection is impractical without hovering — the color encoding reveals little structure at a glance since no sector clusters spatially.
